# `gen.mirror`: Mirror

Adds the mirror image of a mesh across an axis plane, welding the seam; optionally bisects first.

- Category: gen
- Version: 1
- Complexity: O(mesh size) plus O(b log b) for b open-edge vertices near the plane
- Flags: undoable
- Also known as: mirror, mirror modifier, symmetry, reflect, mirror geometry

Keeps the mesh and adds its mirror image across the plane normal to `axis` at `offset`. Open-edge vertices within `weld` of the plane merge with their twins, so a half model built against the plane closes into one piece. `bisect` first cuts the mesh at the plane and keeps one side (`keep_positive`), like `edit.symmetrize`, so parts that cross the plane do not overlap their mirror image.

**Use for** modelling one half of a symmetric prop or character and mirroring it, wheel pairs, left and right panels. For separate mirrored objects use `scene.duplicate` and negate the position instead.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `axis` | `AxisParam` | `"x"` | The axis the mirror plane is normal to (X mirrors left and right). |
| `bisect` | `boolean` | `false` | Cuts the mesh at the plane first and keeps one side, so the halves meet exactly. |
| `keep_positive` | `boolean` | `true` | With bisect: keep the positive side (default) or the negative side. |
| `offset` | `Length` | `0.0` | Where the mirror plane sits along the axis, in object space. |
| `target` | `string` | required | Mesh object (name, path or id). |
| `weld` | `Length` | `0.0001` | Open-edge vertices this close to the plane weld to their mirror twins (0 keeps the seam open). |

## Examples

```json
{"offset":0.3,"target":"crate"}
```

Result: `crate (o:1): mirrored across X at 0.3 m, welded 0 vertices: 12 faces`
